angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 422,290 km at 20.21 pc = 0.28 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 49.4757 +/- 0.0178 mas (same row, RUWE 0.91): 20.21 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.607 +/- 0.014 solar radii from Hobson et al. 2024, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-260 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...688A.216H/abstract): 422,290 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.616 +/- 0.032 solar masses from Hobson et al. 2024, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-260 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...688A.216H/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4026 +/- 14 K from Hobson et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-260 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...688A.216H/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Hobson et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-260 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...688A.216H/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-260.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.661, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
